title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for Florida's 25th Congressional District
description: Florida's 25th Congressional District was significantly redrawn under a new map passed by the Republican-dominated legislature and signed by Governor Ron DeSantis in May 2026, shifting the district from one that narrowly backed Kamala Harris in 2024 to one that Donald Trump won by about 9 points. The seat is open after incumbent Democrat Jared Moskowitz, who previously represented the 23rd District, decided to run in the new 25th, which stretches along Florida's Atlantic coast from Boca Raton to Miami Beach. Both the Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate the newly configured CD-25 as a toss-up, making it one of the most competitive House races in the country in 2026. The Democratic and Republican primaries are scheduled for August 18, 2026, with a crowded GOP field including multiple candidates who followed Moskowitz into the newly drawn district.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 race in Florida's 25th Congressional District as of mid-2026. The race is rated as a toss-up by Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

candidates.name: Jared Moskowitz
candidates.summary: Jared Moskowitz is a Democratic U.S. Representative who currently serves Florida's 23rd Congressional District and is seeking election in the newly redrawn 25th District. A former Florida House member and director of the Florida Division of Emergency Management under Governor Ron DeSantis, Moskowitz has built a reputation as a bipartisan problem-solver and strong voice against antisemitism. He closed the first quarter of 2026 with approximately $1.22 million in cash on hand.

candidates.name: Oliver Larkin
candidates.summary: Oliver Larkin is a Democratic candidate and member of the Democratic Socialists of America challenging incumbent Jared Moskowitz in the Democratic primary for Florida's 25th Congressional District. Larkin previously challenged Moskowitz in the old 23rd District before following him to the newly drawn 25th after redistricting. He announced his campaign via social media, stating that he grew up in the district and currently lives there.

candidates.name: Daniel Franzese
candidates.summary: Daniel Franzese is a Republican candidate for Florida's 25th Congressional District and was the 2024 Republican nominee in Florida's 22nd District. He holds an MBA from the Wharton School and is a businessman who campaigned on affordability, secure borders, and constitutional conservatism. Franzese entered the race for the newly redrawn CD-25 after the 2026 redistricting map was approved.

candidates.name: George Moraitis
candidates.summary: George R. Moraitis Jr. is a Republican candidate and former member of the Florida House of Representatives, where he represented the 93rd District from 2012 to 2020. He previously ran for the old 23rd District before the new map moved him into the 25th.

candidates.name: Scott Singer
candidates.summary: Scott Singer is a Republican candidate and former Mayor of Boca Raton, serving from 2018 to 2026. He pivoted his campaign from the old 23rd District to the newly drawn 25th after the redistricting map was approved.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race as of mid-2026, so confidence is low. The district was significantly redrawn in May 2026 from a Biden +1 seat to a Trump +9 seat, giving Republicans a meaningful structural advantage. However, the Democratic nominee will almost certainly be Jared Moskowitz — a sitting U.S. Representative with $1.22 million cash on hand, high name recognition in the area, and a track record of bipartisan work (including serving as Florida's emergency management director under Governor DeSantis). On the Republican side, a crowded primary field of five candidates (Franzese, Moraitis, Singer, Harrison, Villatoro) remains unresolved ahead of the August 18 primary, creating uncertainty about nominee strength and potential intraparty divisions. Both Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate this open-seat race a toss-up. The best informational forecast is a near-even contest with a very slight edge to Moskowitz given his demonstrated fundraising strength and established profile, partially offsetting the district's redder partisan baseline.
